newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed study ties growth to training - Moskow.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed study ties growth to training - Moskow.

text.p: U.S. Midwest policymakers must foster training, tax incentives and new technologies to ensure strong growth in the region, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Michael Moskow said on Wednesday.

"Fundamental changes in the Midwest economy have put the region on a higher growth path," said Moskow, while presenting the results of a year-long Chicago Fed study on the regional economy, "The Midwest Economy: Looking Back for the Future."
"We can't count on good fortune to continue indefinitely. We've seen in the past how external events can deal setbacks to regions," Moskow cautioned.

The Chicago Fed president said his bank's study provided a "blueprint for action," urging regional policymakers to focus their efforts on three main areas: education and training, tax incentives, and better use of new technology.
Moskow pointed out that the Midwest's "willingness to reinvent itself," was a critical factor in helping the region pull out from the recessions of the early 1980s.
Moskow noted that the Midwest, in the past, was hard hit by recessions due to the high concentration in manufacturing, a sector very sensitive to economic downturns.
"Perhaps, we have broken that pattern," said Moskow, noting that the Midwest led other U.S. regions in emerging from the recession of mid-1990/91.

Moskow also said such changes have led the region's economy to operate "more efficiently, at a world-class standard," but said his bank's study shows key issues still need to be addressed. "The most important lesson for the future is that we were good. That indicates we can influence our destiny by continuing to improve our competitiveness," the Chicago Fed president added.
